questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As I study area-studies, it was important for me to have it be an area of significance. Prague was an interesting middle-ground between the west and the east, so it turned out to be a pretty optimal place for me to go, in order to explore the relationship between western- and Eastern Europe.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The only downside was the EU bureaucracy and administrational bumps on the road.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
I arrived quite early, but the people at Charles Uni have been great at providing information through e-mails
et.al
.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: E-mails, introduction meetings via Zoom, the possibility of getting a 'local buddy' etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I had to contact a friend who's partner is a realtor in Prague. So it wasn't that easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Common sense; be aware of landlords and deposits.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I cannot live in the same room as someone else for a semester, so the lack of private dorms available in Prague was pretty disappointing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The process itself seemed like the exchange students were placed in the last bracket and had to eat the crumbs of the table. Needless to say, very few of us managed to get the courses we had had pre-approved and thus had to change learning agreements during the semester.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
1. Look up courses (open to incoming students, taught language, which faculty etc.)
2. Decide, and have the courses amount to 30 ects
3. Wait until the enrollment begins
4. Pray that you can enroll in time
5. If not, enroll anyway and pray that some people de-enroll and make room for you.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much apart from "just try and wait and see, maybe someone will de-enroll and then you get the spot". And that miraculously worked.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very. I had to give up 5 courses and choose 4 different instead.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be as quick to enroll as possible. And make sure to have a plan B and C in case your first choice courses aren't available.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very satisfied. Great professors and well-structured curricula.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had 5 MA level courses and 1 BA level course. The BA course was relatively easy, while the MA courses resembled what I am used to at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Every professor teach differently, so I cannot compare on university to another. It's individual and also depends on the kind of class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Geopolitics of Great Powers: Russia
- Populism and Democracy
- Historical and Contemporary Geopolitical Issues in Europe
- European Comparative Politics and Society
- Russian Politics and Society
- Symbolical Figures of Czech History

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: My two favourite courses were Populism and Democracy as well as Russian Politics and Society. The professors, Petra Guasti and Karel Svoboda, are two of the most bright, friendly and relevant people I have ever met. And the tro courses themselves were really good too.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The cost of Covid-19 tests when you are not a Czech citizen; around 220DKK for a PCR test.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Meat (especially beef) and cheese was a lot more expensive than expected. Vegetables, bread and public transportation was less expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: CUNI had some good events, however many of them were exclusively in Czech, and following the outbreak of the war in Ukraine, there were very few things we (as incoming, non-Czech students) could do to help.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Help-Ukraine concerts and fundraisers, football / hockey games, karaoke night, pub crawls, weekend-trips around Czechia etc. They did really well.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Emerge yourself in Czech culture; whether it be beer, weird food, traditional customs or other things that set Czechia apart from your own country.
(And explore Prague's techno scene. It's so much fun.)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Definitely go on some day- or weekend trips to Liberec, Plzen, Kutna Kora, Cesky Krumlov etc.
Also, for the hiking/outdoor minded, Slovakia is absolutely stunning.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The language was a barrier; the Czechs usually aren't that good at English. Apart from that, the Czechs aren't very different from the Danes, so it's hard to get into a social circle at first, but once you're inside, it's really great.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and curious about Czechia and their culture.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The architecture as well as the weird mix of Slavic and Germanic cultural traits.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Make sure to have a back up plan for your courses of choice.
2. Spend some weekends away from Prague; I really wish I had taken a few more weekends away than I did.
3. Be open and curious. Some of the people you meet are gonna open up so many options around Europe for you.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's definitely easier to socialize with the Czechs if you like beer!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships and connections, as well as the renewed perspective I now have on my own home country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Sometimes feeling alone and/or isolated. Especially in the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Make sure to go out there, drink a Braník and meet some people! Ná zdraví!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
